Monoclinic sulphur is the reference state of sulphur.
The standard enthalpy of formation of H⁺(aq) is taken as zero by convention.
The standard enthalpy of formation of ozone, O₃(g), is zero.

events.stem:
Standard enthalpy of formation (ΔfH°) values are defined with respect to elements in their most stable reference states at 298.15 K and 1 bar.
Which of the following statements about standard enthalpies of formation is/are correct? (One or more options may be correct.)
(A) Rhombic sulphur is the reference state of sulphur.
(B) Monoclinic sulphur is the reference state of sulphur.
(C) The standard enthalpy of formation of H⁺(aq) is taken as zero by convention.
(D) The standard enthalpy of formation of ozone, O₃(g), is zero.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working: Standard enthalpy of formation ΔfH° is defined relative to elements in their most stable reference states at 298.15 K and 1 bar. For sulphur, the most stable solid form at these conditions is rhombic sulphur (S8(s) network), not monoclinic sulphur. Therefore (A) is correct and (B) is incorrect. By convention, the standard enthalpy of formation of H+(aq) is taken as zero because it is defined relative to the element hydrogen in its standard state (H2(g)), and the convention sets ΔfH°(H+(aq)) = 0. Thus (C) is correct. Ozone O3(g) is not an element; its standard enthalpy of formation is not zero (ΔfH°(O3(g)) ≈ 142 kJ·mol⁻¹). Hence (D) is incorrect. The correct statements are (A) and (C).

chain.description: the Maxwell distribution of molecular speeds

values.lead: Which of the following statements about the Maxwell distribution of molecular speeds is/are correct? (One or more options may be correct.)
options: For a fixed number of molecules, the area under the distribution curve does not change with temperature.
At the same temperature, a lighter gas has its distribution peak at a higher speed than a heavier gas.
At the same temperature, a heavier gas has its distribution peak at a higher speed than a lighter gas.
The most probable speed is smaller than the average speed, which is smaller than the root-mean-square speed.

events.stem:
Consider an ideal gas sample containing a fixed number of molecules.
Which of the following statements about the Maxwell distribution of molecular speeds is/are correct? (One or more options may be correct.)
(A) For a fixed number of molecules, the area under the distribution curve does not change with temperature.
(B) At the same temperature, a lighter gas has its distribution peak at a higher speed than a heavier gas.
(C) At the same temperature, a heavier gas has its distribution peak at a higher speed than a lighter gas.
(D) The most probable speed is smaller than the average speed, which is smaller than the root-mean-square speed.
